Top 10 Universal Tensile Machines (UTM) for Chemical Labs
December 8, 2024
The chemical industry is evolving rapidly, and there have been recent breakthroughs in sustainable plastics, advanced composites, and other innovative materials. Testing these materials for strength, flexibility, and durability is essential for meeting rigorous safety and performance standards. In laboratories around the world, Universal Tensile Machines (UTMs) provide the precise measurements necessary for these evaluations.
Research shows that the global tensile testing machine market, valued at approximately USD 561.8 million in 2023, is expected to reach USD 817.25 million by 2032. This growth reflects how essential UTMs have become for chemical labs, where exacting standards demand tools capable of delivering precise, dependable results.
What sets UTMs apart today is their ability to integrate with materials informatics solutions like MaterialsZone. These systems turn raw testing data into actionable insights and help labs innovate faster while minimizing errors. Let's look at the top ten Universal Tensile Machines and what they can bring to your lab.
What Are Universal Tensile Machines (UTM)?
Universal Tensile Machines (UTMs) are highly specialized instruments that are designed to evaluate the mechanical properties of materials. These machines perform a range of tests, such as tension, compression, bending, and shear, to measure characteristics like strength, elasticity, and deformation. Their versatility makes them an essential tool in material science and engineering.
UTMs are commonly used to test polymers, metals, ceramics, and composites, making them invaluable across industries like aerospace, automotive, and manufacturing. In chemical laboratories, UTMs play a crucial role in ensuring that materials meet rigorous performance standards. They provide precise data on tensile strength and other properties, which helps labs validate material reliability and suitability for specific applications.
In chemical labs, UTMs are vital for research and development, and offer unique insights that drive material innovation. Their accurate and repeatable results allow researchers to refine formulations, enhance performance, and ensure compliance with industry regulations.
When connected to materials informatics platforms like MaterialsZone, UTMs deliver a strategic advantage by providing raw data that are transformed into actionable insights. Chemical labs leverage these insights to streamline workflows, reduce errors, and accelerate the development of advanced materials. This synergy positions UTMs as a critical tool in modern material science.
Types of Universal Tensile Machines
Universal Tensile Machines for chemical labs come in several types, each suited to specific materials and testing scenarios: 
Electromechanical UTMs
Designed for precision, these machines use electric motors to control force with exceptional accuracy. They excel in low-force applications, such as testing thin films, lightweight plastics, and elastomers, where even minor measurements matter.
Hydraulic UTMs
Built for high-load testing, hydraulic UTMs handle robust materials like metals and composites. Known for their durability and reliability, these machines are ideal for applications requiring extreme force testing in industrial environments.
Servo-Hydraulic UTMs
Combining hydraulic strength with electronic control, servo-hydraulic UTMs are perfect for dynamic testing scenarios. They are used to simulate real-world conditions where forces fluctuate, making them invaluable for testing automotive parts and structural components.
Tabletop UTMs
Compact and efficient tabletop UTMs are designed for labs with limited space. Despite their size, they provide reliable results, making them an excellent choice for small samples or educational settings.
Benefits of Universal Tensile Machines (UTM)
Universal Tensile Machines offer many benefits to chemical lab professionals, including:
Precision and Reliability - UTMs provide consistent and accurate results, whether for R&D or quality control. Their precision eliminates guesswork and enables faster product optimization and greater data confidence.
Regulatory Compliance - UTMs generate detailed, replicable data that simplifies adherence to regulatory standards and ensures materials meet stringent chemical industry safety requirements.
Accelerated Innovation - Integrating UTMs with materials informatics platforms like MaterialsZone allows labs to analyze testing data to identify trends, optimize materials, and innovate faster with less trial and error.
Cost Efficiency - UTMs reduce the risk of costly production errors by proactively catching material weaknesses early in the testing phase—saving time, minimizing waste, and lowering operational costs.
Versatility - From testing the tensile strength of biodegradable plastics to the compressive force of aerospace composites, UTMs are flexible and can handle a wide variety of applications.
Key Features of Universal Tensile Machines (UTM)
When selecting the right Universal Tensile Machine (UTM) for your lab, it’s essential to evaluate key features that align with your testing needs. Here are some important aspects to consider:
Materials informatics platforms.
Preventive safeguards to ensure operator and equipment safety.
Top 10 Universal Tensile Machines (UTM) for Chemical Labs
1. Shimadzu AGX-V Series
The Shimadzu AGX-V Series combines advanced control systems with high-rigidity frames, making it ideal for chemical labs testing polymers, elastomers, and composites. With ultra-high-speed data sampling at 10 kHz and intelligent crosshead positioning, it ensures accurate results. Automation features include programmable test sequences for consistent operations and minimized manual intervention.
‍Best for: Chemical labs requiring precise testing of polymers and composites with advanced data analysis and safety capabilities.
2. ZwickRoell AllroundLine
The ZwickRoell AllroundLine is a versatile universal testing machine available in both floor-standing and tabletop models, with load capacities ranging from 5 kN to 250 kN. Its modular design allows for customized configurations, including options for multiple test areas and integration with temperature chambers, catering to diverse testing requirements. 
‍Best for: Chemical labs seeking a flexible testing machine that can handle a wide range of materials and test types, from quality control to advanced research applications.
3. Instron 6800 Series
The Instron 6800 Series offers universal testing systems with capacities from 500 N to 300 kN, providing exceptional accuracy and reliability. With up to 5 kHz data acquisition and ±0.5% accuracy down to 1/1000th of load cell capacity, they perform tensile, compression, flexure, peel, puncture, friction, and shear tests. 
‍Best for: Chemical labs requiring versatile testing capabilities across various materials and applications, with high precision and adaptability.
4. MTS Criterion Series
The MTS Criterion® Electromechanical Test Systems offer force capacities from 1 to 600 kN, featuring high-speed, low-vibration electromechanical drives and integrated digital closed-loop controls for precise material testing. With a data acquisition rate of up to 5000 Hz, they provide accurate measurements essential for chemical labs.
‍Best for: Chemical laboratories requiring versatile and precise testing of various materials, including polymers and composites, with high data fidelity.
5. ADMET eXpert 7600 Series
The ADMET eXpert 7600 Series is a compact, single-column testing system capable of performing tension, compression, flexure, and peel/adhesion tests. With force capacities up to 5 kN and the industry's largest vertical test space, it's ideal for high-elongation materials. It’s customizable with various grips, fixtures, and environmental systems. 
‍Best for: Chemical labs requiring a space-efficient, versatile testing machine for materials like thin films, elastomers, and adhesives.
6. Tinius Olsen Universal Testing Machines
The Tinius Olsen ST Series comprises floor-standing universal testing machines with capacities of 100 kN, 150 kN, and 300 kN. The ST Series can test a wide range of materials, including plastics, films, paper, packaging materials, adhesives, and medical devices, in tension, compression, flexure, shear, and peel. They feature high precision, interchangeable strain gauge load cells for capturing applied load data, and can operate at speeds ranging from 0.001 mm/min to 500 mm/min.
‍Best for: Chemical labs requiring versatile testing capabilities for a diverse array of materials, with a focus on precision and adaptability.
7. Testometric X500 Series
‍Testometric's X500 Series features twin-column, bench-mounted universal testing machines with precision AC servo drive systems and full computer control. With capacities up to 100 kN, they offer high-speed operation and precise crosshead guidance, making them ideal for demanding material testing applications. 
‍Best for: Chemical labs requiring versatile, high-capacity testing solutions for various materials, including polymers and composites.
8. Lloyd Instruments LD Series
The Lloyd Instruments LD Series testing machines offer bench-mounted universal testing machines with capacities ranging from 5 kN to 100 kN. Featuring a high-stiffness frame and an advanced AC drive system, they ensure precise tension, compression, and flexure testing. The expansive working area and customizable configurations accommodate diverse material testing needs. 
‍Best for: Chemical labs seeking versatile, high-precision testing equipment for a wide range of materials and applications.
9. Torontech TTM-Series 
The Torontech TTM-Series Electromechanical Universal Testing Machines offer capacities from low benchtop configurations up to 1,000 kN in floor-standing models. They support various accessories, including grips, fixtures, compression plates, thermal cabinets, and extensometers, enabling comprehensive testing of metals, plastics, textiles, and more. 
‍Best for: Chemical labs seeking versatile testing solutions with customizable configurations to meet specific testing requirements.
10. United Testing Systems SSTM Series
The United Electromechanical DSTM Series Tensile Testing System offers versatile testing capabilities for tension, compression, flexure, and shear applications. With force capacities up to 100 kN, it features a dual-column design and advanced digital controls for precise measurements. The system supports various grips and fixtures to accommodate diverse material testing needs. 
‍Best for: Chemical labs requiring a robust and adaptable testing system for a wide range of materials, including polymers and composites.
